clue.text: Train starts to puff really oddly with constant, strange noises

indicators.note: something strange is out of its usual order, so the next word is rearranged
the starts of the following words are their opening letters only

parts.note: the first letters of these three words
C is the usual symbol for a constant, such as the speed of light
these six letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A steam train chugs along, puffing erratically and making constant odd noises.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Train' looks like a locomotive, but here it is a line of people moving in order. 'oddly' belongs to the surface, not to the letter picking.
explanation.definitionFit: A train can mean a long line of followers or attendants moving along, which is what a procession is.

clue.text: Wan friend with little energy

parts.note: a pal is a friend
E is the abbreviation for energy, and 'little' signals the short form

explanation.surface: A friend who looks wan because they have hardly any energy left.
explanation.definitionFit: Wan and pale are synonyms for a face lacking colour, often through illness or tiredness.

clue.text: Group of players chat and Roger's upset, abandoning golf

indicators.note: upset things are knocked over and jumbled, so the letters are rearranged
abandoning something means leaving it behind, so that letter drops out

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, with the S of the possessive
golf is G in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A sports team talks while Roger sulks about having to give up his golf.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the G from CHAT plus ROGERS, then rearrange the remaining nine letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An orchestra is an ensemble of musicians, players in the musical rather than sporting sense.

clue.text: Old person in Daniel Deronda

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the run of words that follows

parts.note: spans the end of the first name and start of the surname

explanation.surface: Pointing out an elderly character in George Eliot's novel Daniel Deronda.
explanation.walkthrough: Daniel Deronda is George Eliot's last novel; the title is only a carrier for the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An elder is an older person, especially one respected for age and experience.

clue.text: Sign of nerves, maybe, Harry has with Charles?

indicators.note: to harry is to harass or disturb, so the following word is rearranged

parts.note: these three letters rearranged
Charles III is the current British king

explanation.surface: Is Prince Harry nervous when he is with his father King Charles?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Harry' reads as the prince's name, but it is the verb meaning to harass.
explanation.definitionFit: Trembling hands or a shaky voice are a typical symptom of nervousness, hence 'maybe'.

clue.text: Fruit bats go near bottom of plants

indicators.note: bats is slang for crazy, so the words after it are scrambled

parts.note: these six letters rearranged

indicators.note: the bottom of a word written downwards is its last letter

parts.note: the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: Fruit bats flying in close to the base of the plants they feed on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fruit bats' is a real animal, but the phrase splits: 'Fruit' is the definition and 'bats' the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Oranges are citrus fruits, so the plural noun is an example of the general category.

clue.text: Try second pill

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for second
a tab is short for tablet, a pill

explanation.surface: Have a go at taking a second pill.
explanation.definitionFit: To have a stab at something is an idiom for making an attempt, so a stab is a try.

clue.text: Greek character — he enters dry area

indicators.note: entering means going inside, so this pronoun is placed within the other letters

parts.note: TT means teetotal, so not drinking
A is the abbreviation for area
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Greek man walks into a dry area, perhaps a desert.
explanation.walkthrough: HE goes between the two Ts of TT, followed by A. TT stands for teetotal.
explanation.definitionFit: Theta is the eighth letter of the Greek alphabet, and a letter is a character.

clue.text: Ben's issues — worrying concerns

indicators.note: worrying at something is tugging it about, so the letters are pulled into a new order

parts.note: all ten letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Ben has some troubles, which are worrying matters for him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'concerns' looks like a synonym for worries, matching the surface, but it means firms.
explanation.definitionFit: A concern is a commercial enterprise or firm, so businesses are concerns.

clue.text: Sweets son found in ditches

indicators.note: something found in something else sits inside it

parts.note: to ditch someone is to desert them
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: Sweets belonging to a son discovered lying in roadside ditches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ditches' reads as a noun for trenches but is the verb meaning abandons.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweets is a British word for puddings or desserts served at the end of a meal.

clue.text: Eloquent university student kept back by group of detectives

indicators.note: kept back suggests being turned the other way, so these letters run right to left

parts.note: U is the abbreviation for university
L is a learner, as on British learner-driver plates
the Criminal Investigation Department of the British police

explanation.surface: A well-spoken undergraduate is held for questioning by plain-clothes police.
explanation.walkthrough: CID is the detective branch of British police; L for learner stands in for any student.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucid means clearly expressed, and an eloquent speaker communicates with that clarity.

clue.text: Understanding answer as clue, finally, is cracked

indicators.note: something cracked is broken apart, so these letters are reassembled differently

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word before it

parts.note: the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A solver grasps that a clue has finally been cracked and the answer found.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is about solving crosswords, but 'answer' and 'as' are fodder, not meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: Awareness is knowledge or comprehension of a situation, a synonym for understanding as a noun.

clue.text: Craving yen before getting paid

parts.note: Y is the abbreviation for yen, the Japanese currency
earning is getting paid for work

explanation.surface: Longing for the yen one earns before payday arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'yen' also means a longing, which suits the surface, but here it is the currency.
explanation.definitionFit: Craving and yearning both mean an intense desire for something, used as nouns or participles.

clue.text: Bridge crossing island somewhere in Europe

indicators.note: a bridge crossing something spans over it, so one piece goes around the other

parts.note: a span is a bridge or arch
I is the abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: A bridge crosses over to an island in some European country.
explanation.definitionFit: Spain is a country in south-western Europe, so it is one example of a place there.

clue.text: Food urges following alcohol

indicators.note: following means coming after, so the first word of the pair is sent to the back

parts.note: Scotch is whisky
to egg someone on is to urge them

explanation.surface: Cravings for something to eat after a night's drinking.
explanation.walkthrough: A Scotch egg is a hard-boiled egg wrapped in sausage meat and breadcrumbs, a British picnic snack; Scotch here is whisky.
explanation.definitionFit: Scotch eggs are a snack food, so the general word covers them as an example.

clue.text: Hurtful piece from a newspaper?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: wounding, as a remark can be
second meaning: an article clipped out of the paper

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark hints that a newspaper piece might be unkind, but the two halves are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: A cutting remark is wounding, and a press cutting is a clipping removed from a newspaper.

clue.text: Set of books finished after I planned

indicators.note: after places the pronoun just before it at the front, with the rest of the pieces behind

parts.note: taken as written
NT is the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible
ended means finished

explanation.surface: I had planned to finish reading a collection of books.
explanation.walkthrough: NT, the New Testament, is a standard crossword 'set of books'; the Bible's two testaments are each a collection.
explanation.definitionFit: Intended and planned are synonymous adjectives or past participles for something meant or designed.

clue.text: What could be seen on admiral's journey east in ship

definitions.text: What could be seen on admiral

indicators.note: in places what precedes it inside the abbreviation that follows

parts.note: SS is steamship
a trip is a journey
E is the abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: An admiral makes a voyage eastwards aboard a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'admiral's' sets up the sea scene, but the definition is the gold bands on an admiral's sleeve, or perhaps the red admiral butterfly's markings.
explanation.definitionFit: Naval officers' rank is shown by gold stripes on the cuff, and an admiral wears several.

clue.text: Piece of text from Standard article put on chart

parts.note: par is the standard or normal level
A is the indefinite article
a graph is a chart

explanation.surface: A passage lifted from the Evening Standard newspaper, with an article printed alongside a chart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put on' just says what comes next. The Standard is a London newspaper, which steers the solver away from par.
explanation.definitionFit: A paragraph is a distinct section of writing, so it is a piece of a longer text.

clue.text: Farmer might make use of this rat after a change of heart

definitions.text: Farmer might make use of this

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its middle letter, and changing it swaps it for a different one

parts.note: a rat is a betrayer or turncoat

explanation.surface: A farmer might find use for this rodent once it has a change of heart.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle letter I of TRAITOR becomes C. The clue does not say which letter replaces it; the definition and crossers settle that.
explanation.definitionFit: A tractor is the vehicle a farmer uses to pull ploughs and other machinery.

clue.text: Lie about Conservative policy

parts.note: re means about or concerning
C is the abbreviation for Conservative
a party line is its policy

explanation.surface: Accusing someone of being untruthful about Tory policy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lie' suggests a falsehood, but it is the verb meaning to lie back.
explanation.definitionFit: To recline is to lie or lean back in a relaxed position.

clue.text: Rate heads of department eventually work for

indicators.note: the heads of words are their first letters

parts.note: the opening letter of each of these two words
to serve someone is to work for them

explanation.surface: Grading the department managers who will in time work for you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rate' looks like a noun or a judgement verb; here it means to merit.
explanation.definitionFit: To rate something can mean to be worth or merit it, as in 'he rates a mention'.

clue.text: Father capturing sorcerer gets harmed

indicators.note: capturing someone means holding them inside, so one word surrounds another

parts.note: dad is father
a mage is a magician or sorcerer

explanation.surface: A father who catches a wizard ends up hurt in the struggle.
explanation.definitionFit: Damaged and harmed are synonyms describing something injured or impaired.

clue.text: Chicken trapping rook and old wading bird

indicators.note: trapping something means enclosing it, so the bird's letters go around the rest

parts.note: a hen is a chicken
R is rook in chess notation
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: A chicken traps a rook and some old wading bird in the farmyard.
explanation.walkthrough: R and O both go inside HEN; 'and' links the two pieces being trapped. 'rook' is the chess piece, not the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The heron is a long-legged bird that stands in shallow water to catch fish.

clue.text: Angry rodent heartlessly shot

indicators.note: without a heart means the central letter is removed

parts.note: a rat is a rodent
to have a shot is to have a try

explanation.surface: A rodent that has been callously shot.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the middle R from TRY. Ratty is informal British for irritable.
explanation.definitionFit: Ratty is a colloquial British word for bad-tempered or irritable.

clue.text: Military operation affected by American GI returning note

parts.note: camp means theatrically affected or exaggerated
A is the abbreviation for American

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the letters are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: taken as written
N is the abbreviation for note

explanation.surface: A military operation in which an American soldier is moved by a returning letter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'affected by' looks like one idea, but 'affected' is a piece in its own right, meaning showy.
explanation.definitionFit: A campaign is a connected series of military actions aimed at a goal in a war.

clue.text: Change headgear on animal? Not hard!

indicators.note: not means take away, and hard is the abbreviation that goes

parts.note: a halter is a rope or strap fitted over a horse's head
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Putting a hat on an animal is an easy change to make.
explanation.definitionFit: To alter something is to change or modify it; the two verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Bird wanting tail cut off

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so the final letter of the bird is missing

parts.note: a snipe is a long-billed wading bird

explanation.surface: A bird missing its tail, which has been chopped off.
explanation.definitionFit: To snip is to cut something off with a small quick stroke of the scissors.

clue.text: Understanding group of people

definitions.meaning: second meaning: an assembly or meeting

explanation.walkthrough: 'Understanding' reads as a noun, but it is the participle of the verb meaning to infer.
explanation.definitionFit: To gather is to infer or work out, and a gathering is an assembly of people.

clue.text: US writer's tango with Marian regularly ignored

parts.note: tango is T in the NATO phonetic alphabet
W is the abbreviation for with

indicators.note: ignoring every other letter in a regular rhythm leaves only the alternate ones

parts.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters

explanation.surface: An American author dances the tango with a woman called Marian, whom he then snubs.
explanation.walkthrough: Mark Twain, author of Huckleberry Finn, was the pen name of Samuel Clemens.
explanation.definitionFit: Mark Twain is a celebrated American novelist and humorist, so he is an example of a US writer.

clue.text: Ask a gypsy regularly for comments

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, taking every second letter

parts.note: the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters

explanation.surface: Ask a fortune teller for her remarks on a regular basis.
explanation.definitionFit: Comments and says are both verbs meaning remarks or states aloud an opinion.

clue.text: What we might expect from the government Starmer's in?

definitions.text: What we might expect from the government Starmer's in?

parts.words: What we might expect from the government
parts.note: surface reading: the quality voters hope a government shows, direction from the top
setter's reading: Starmer is the party leader, so the vessel he governs is the leader's ship

explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as LEADER'S HIP and then as LEADER'S SHIP; the 'government' Keir Starmer is in, as Labour leader, is the leader's vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Leadership is the act of guiding a group, the thing voters hope a government will provide.
